payload.detail: u_orange drifted relative to the gripper TCP while held

payload.explanation: slip_u_orange fired at trigger_wall_ns 1792532531881950000, observed drift 0.02115m against the 0.02m grasp_slip_tolerance_m threshold (raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m, verified). I pulled object_poses(u_orange) and frames(tcp) over 1792532529000000000-1792532532500000000 to characterize the mechanism rather than just report the breach. While held and in transit (u_orange's z was still ~0.075-0.16m, well above its u_orange_placement z of 0.0454m, so this was not yet the seating moment), the object-to-TCP separation shrank steadily from its stable in-transit value of ~0.0911m (matching the constant offset seen for u_brown's own carry, consistent with a fixed grasp geometry) down to ~0.0697m by the time of the fire, and u_orange's orientation quaternion began rotating away from its earlier near-constant value in the same window. A rigidly held part preserves both the TCP-object distance and relative orientation; both changed together here, which is the signature of the part shifting/rotating in the gripper's grasp (a partial slip) rather than sensor noise or normal carry motion. No other requirement was affected by this: base1 and the other bystanders' stillness monitors did not fire, and u_brown's post-placement stillness monitor did not fire, so the slip was isolated to u_orange in the gripper. This finding stands at the time of this step; the part's seating at its own milestone (place_u_orange) will still be checked independently against the placement frame regardless of this slip, since a slip does not by itself determine whether the part is later re-seated correctly.

payload.reason: still_u_brown_post and still_base1 both fired right after pick_line_green began, with u_brown's evidence showing a sudden non-physical jump far off the table; confirming current scene state visually

payload.explanation: Two monitors fired within ~0.1s of each other, both at tf_stamp_ns 299258348940, right after begin_step pick_line_green (object_ids=["line_green"]; u_brown and base1 were not named, so both should have stayed put). still_u_brown_post fired with observed drift 0.1049m (threshold 0.02m); still_base1 fired with observed drift 0.02629m (threshold 0.02m, agent-sourced from raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m since base1 carries no contract of its own). I pulled object_poses(u_brown, base1) bracketing the fires: u_brown's pose was static for the entire preceding ~2.4s, then in a single 50ms tick jumped from (0.401,-0.158,0.043) to (0.455,-0.079,0.098) with a full orientation discontinuity, and continued accelerating away over the following ticks, reaching (0.480,1.84,0.54) -- off the bench entirely -- by the end of the window I pulled, with no skill_start/skill_end event from the executor in that span. A look() taken afterward confirms u_brown is no longer visible anywhere on the bench or in base1's fixture holes. base1 jumped in the same tick (small position shift plus a transient ~7-8 degree rotation) but then settled back to within 0.018m of its reference by 708978760400, i.e. it recovered after the transient. The absence of any commanded skill event, the single-tick discontinuity, and the explosive divergence of u_brown's trajectory are the signature of a physics-constraint resolution event (most likely residual interpenetration left over from u_orange's earlier misseated first placement attempt, which came to rest close to u_brown before being corrected, being violently resolved once physics re-settled) rather than anything the executor commanded. I cannot observe contact forces directly to confirm this mechanism with certainty, so I report it as the most plausible explanation given the evidence rather than a confirmed cause. Regardless of mechanism, both u_brown (already past its milestone, required to stay seated) and base1 (the fixture, must never move) exceeded their disturbance tolerances, so this is a conformance violation independent of fault attribution. u_brown's current pose is far outside any tolerance of its placement frame and remains unresolved as of this record.

payload.summary: u_brown underwent an unexplained, non-physical displacement (single-tick ~0.1m jump with full orientation flip, then continued moving away to roughly (0.48, 1.84, 0.54) in world frame, off the bench) with no corresponding commanded skill event; base1 also jumped transiently in the same tick before settling back near its original pose.
payload.impact_detail: Recorded as a non_conformant finding under step pick_line_green (undisturbed_inactive_part and base1_undisturbed clauses).

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict. Process: u_brown -> u_orange -> line_green -> inverted_u_yellow, in order. I measured each part's final pose against its own placement frame from my own evidence (query_snapshot) at run end, independent of the executor's claims.

Timeline: pick_u_brown and place_u_brown closed clean (effort 61.09/100, lift 0.2m, seated 0.0027m within 0.01m tolerance, base1 undisturbed). During place_approach_u_orange, slip_u_orange fired (drift 0.02115m > 0.02m tolerance) -- recorded as a finding; evidence showed the object-TCP offset and orientation both drifting together, the signature of in-gripper slip. The executor's own verification then caught the resulting misseat (28.5mm/20.6deg off) at place_u_orange, re-grasped, and reseated u_orange successfully (final error 0.00205m within 0.02m) without disturbing u_brown (0.00738m, within 0.02m) -- a genuine recovery of that specific fault. Immediately after, at the start of pick_line_green, two monitors fired in the same tick: u_brown -- already seated and verified -- underwent a sudden, non-physical ~0.1m single-tick jump with a full orientation discontinuity and no corresponding commanded skill event, continuing to diverge afterward to an unreachable pose (~5.1m from its placement, confirmed missing from the fixture by both my own look() and the executor's own camera check); base1 also jumped transiently (0.02629m, over its 0.02m tolerance) before partially settling back to within 0.018m of its start, though its orientation never returned to its original near-identity value (now ~7.8 degrees rotated) and placement frames for u_orange/line_green/inverted_u_yellow moved rigidly with it. I could not observe contact forces directly to confirm a cause; the single-tick discontinuity and absence of any commanded motion point most plausibly to a physics-engine constraint-resolution event (likely residual interpenetration left from u_orange's earlier misseated first attempt, which rested close to u_brown before correction), reported as the most likely mechanism rather than a certainty. Both findings were recorded immediately as non_conformant under step pick_line_green. line_green itself was picked and seated cleanly afterward (0.0066m within 0.015m). The executor then detected u_brown's situation itself, queried the scene, attempted to move toward recovery, found u_brown unreachable, and called run_ended with status aborted; inverted_u_yellow was never attempted and remains at its original resting pose, nowhere near its placement frame.

End-state measured now (tagged under place_line_green, the last step to close before the run ended): u_brown is 5.11m from u_brown_placement (threshold 0.01m) -- a standing, uncorrected violation. u_orange is 0.0063m from u_orange_placement (within 0.02m) -- conformant. line_green is 0.0066m from line_green_placement (within 0.015m) -- conformant. inverted_u_yellow was never attempted and sits 0.17m from its placement frame, far outside its 0.012m tolerance -- not seated. base1's position is 0.0178m from its original reference (within my agent-chosen 0.02m observation threshold, base1 has no contract of its own) but its orientation is permanently altered (~7.8deg) from its start, so the disturbance is not fully corrected even though position recovered.

Because a violation (u_brown's catastrophic displacement) stands uncorrected at run end, the verdict is non_conformant regardless of the run having aborted and regardless of u_orange's slip having been successfully recovered. The slip-and-recovery episode on u_orange is a genuine partial recovery within an otherwise non_conformant run; it does not by itself determine the run's end-state, which is set by u_brown's standing violation and inverted_u_yellow never having been reached.
